chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man who had no wealth, and a man from his brothers financed his Hajj. Does that suffice for him in place of the Hajj of Islam (Fard), or is it incomplete? He said: 'Rather, it is a complete Hajj.'

key_terms.حَجَّ بِهِ: Financed his Hajj / Paid for his Hajj

ai.seo_question: Does a financed Hajj count as the obligatory Hajj for the poor person?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that financial sponsorship by another person fully satisfies the condition of ability (*istita'ah*) for the obligatory Hajj, rendering it complete rather than deficient. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the obligation rests on the individual's capacity to perform the ritual, which can be met through external support, thereby ensuring accessibility for the less fortunate. It highlights the communal responsibility in fulfilling one of the pillars of Islam, reinforcing the social dimension of religious duty.
